gaps.sentence: 'Don't forget your tickets,' she said to us. She ___ us to take our tickets.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't forget' maps onto remind + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: "I will call you tomorrow." — She said she ___ me the next day.
'When did the ancient city fall?' we asked the guide. We asked the guide when the ancient city ___.
gaps.explanation: did...fall → had fallen: the auxiliary 'did' disappears and the verb backshifts.

gaps.sentence: 'Which seat do you prefer?' the steward asked. The steward asked which seat I ___.
gaps.explanation: do you prefer → I preferred: statement order, present simple backshifted.

gaps.sentence: 'We stayed at this hotel last summer,' they recalled. They recalled that they had stayed at ___ hotel the summer before.
gaps.explanation: Demonstratives shift: this hotel → that hotel; last summer → the summer before.

gaps.sentence: 'I will always love you,' he whispered. He whispered that he ___ always love me.
gaps.explanation: Will backshifts to would; 'you' shifts to 'me' from the speaker's new perspective.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll have finished by noon,' she promised. She promised she ___ finished by noon.
gaps.explanation: will have + past participle becomes would have + past participle.

gaps.sentence: "I am sorry I am late." — He ___ for being late.
gaps.explanation: 'Apologise for doing something' reports an apology.
